projectSubtitle: Missed events, duplicate processing, checkpoint recovery, RPC interruptions, transaction confirmations and chain reorganizations
projectStatus: Independent reference implementation prepared for scope discussion. Synthetic data only. Not a production system, and not the code of any client or company.
proposedRole: External Web3 infrastructure reviewer: reads the sandbox, checks it against the listed invariants and failure scenarios, and reports prioritized findings

implementedComponents.name: Deterministic EVM fixture chain
implementedComponents.description: Seeded blocks, ERC-20 Transfer and SettlementRecorded logs, reorganizations and branch switching, a fault-injectable provider and a head notifier that can drop, repeat and disconnect.

implementedComponents.name: Event identity and deduplication
implementedComponents.description: Identity (chainId, blockHash, transactionHash, logIndex) enforced by a primary key and a unique constraint; insert-if-absent writes; derived state follows the rows actually changed.

implementedComponents.name: Durable checkpoint and single-writer fencing
implementedComponents.description: Checkpoint in PostgreSQL that moves only with the data it describes; per-chain row lock plus a fencing version so several workers are safe.

implementedComponents.name: Range scanner with backfill and bounded retries
implementedComponents.description: Derives progress from stored state and block ranges, treats head notifications as hints only, validates every provider answer, retries transient errors with bounded back-off, halts instead of guessing.

implementedComponents.name: Confirmation lifecycle
implementedComponents.description: observed -> provisional -> confirmed | orphaned, with a configurable depth measured from the durable checkpoint.

implementedComponents.name: Reorganization detection, correction and escalation
implementedComponents.description: Common-ancestor search, atomic and idempotent correction of events and derived state, audit trail, incidents for orphaned confirmed events, halt beyond the automatic rollback limit.

implementedComponents.name: Transactional outbox, Redis Streams delivery and idempotent consumer
implementedComponents.description: Notification intent written in the confirming transaction; publisher with SKIP LOCKED; consumer group with pending recovery and XAUTOCLAIM; effect committed before acknowledgement; re-queue after broker data loss; local notification sink.

implementedComponents.name: Stored-state invariant checker
implementedComponents.description: Twelve SQL invariants re-derived from PostgreSQL, run after every scenario and available at GET /status?verify=true.

implementedComponents.name: Local API with OpenAPI
implementedComponents.description: Fastify routes with request validation: /healthz, /status, /events, /events/:id, /alerts, /scenarios, /scenarios/:id, /metrics, /openapi.json; guarded admin and fault-injection routes disabled by default.

implementedComponents.name: Executable failure scenarios S01-S09 and demo
implementedComponents.description: Each scenario has a deterministic fixture, fault injection, expected behavior, an executable test, observable evidence and declared pass/fail checks; a CLI runner and a narrated demo.

implementedComponents.name: Continuous integration
implementedComponents.description: Typecheck, lint, unit tests, integration and fault-injection tests against real PostgreSQL and Redis, the scenario suite, on Node 22 and 24; fails if any test or scenario is skipped.

proposedComponents.name: Read-only JSON-RPC provider adapter
proposedComponents.description: An implementation of the ChainProvider interface for a real node, disabled by default, including eth_getLogs range and size limits.

proposedComponents.name: Multi-provider head and ancestor comparison
proposedComponents.description: Cross-checking heads, headers and common ancestors across providers, with jittered back-off and a circuit breaker.

proposedComponents.name: Finality-aware confirmation
proposedComponents.description: Using safe / finalized block tags alongside the configured depth.

proposedComponents.name: Silent-gap detection
proposedComponents.description: Cross-checking returned logs against the header's logs bloom or receipts, or a second source, so an incomplete log range is detected without waiting for a replay.

proposedComponents.name: Poison-message handling
proposedComponents.description: Delivery cap and dead-letter stream for messages that keep failing.

proposedComponents.name: Native and internal transfer identity
proposedComponents.description: Event kinds and keys for native-value and trace-level transfers, kept separate from contract logs.

proposedComponents.name: Retention and partitioning
proposedComponents.description: Pruning or partitioning of blocks, audit rows and outbox rows; trimming of the Redis stream.

proposedComponents.name: Webhook sink with idempotency key
proposedComponents.description: An HTTP delivery target that deduplicates on the notification id, tested against a local receiver.

proposedComponents.name: Operator tooling
proposedComponents.description: Resolving payload-mismatch incidents, re-driving a single notification, a guarded manual rollback.

proposedComponents.name: Container restart tests
proposedComponents.description: Restarting the Redis and PostgreSQL containers during a scenario instead of simulating the loss.

deliverables: A written technical review of the sandbox against docs/reliability-invariants.md and the review questions in docs/review-guide.md, with findings ranked by severity and each tied to evidence or to a proposed failing test.
A prioritized list of failure modes the nine scenarios do not cover, each with a proposed deterministic scenario.
Recommendations on the open points in docs/known-limitations.md, in particular multi-provider operation, finality and silent-gap detection.
One handover call to walk through the findings.
outOfScope: Production deployment, operation or monitoring of any system
Custody, wallets, signing, private keys or key management
Trading, execution, or any transaction on a live network
Paid RPC providers or any credentials
Unpaid implementation work on the sandbox
compensationStatus: Paid, fixed-scope review. Actual fee: not yet agreed. Final terms: subject to written agreement.
knownLimitations: Single synthetic provider; no quorum or failover between providers
Confirmation by depth only; safe / finalized tags are not read
No automatic detection of an incomplete log range from a consistent provider; a replay heals a gap once someone looks
No poison-message handling or dead-letter stream
No pruning or partitioning; Redis stream is not trimmed
Native-value and internal transfers are not implemented
Redis restart is simulated (stream deleted, workers SIGKILLed), not performed on a container
No performance, throughput or uptime measurements
Read API is unauthenticated and bound to loopback by default
